question: How can my company register as a tenderer on e-GP?
expected_section: Steps for registering on e-GP Portal / Flow of the Registration Process
expected_answer: Go to https://eprocure.gov.bd, click “New User Registration”. Enter a unique email ID (this becomes Login-ID), create a password (min 8 characters with both alphabets and numbers), select Hint Question/Answer, Nationality, Registration Type (Tenderer/Consultant, Individual Consultant, Government Owned Enterprise, or Media), Country of Business, enter Captcha, accept Terms & Conditions, and Submit. An email with verification code is sent. Verify email within 72 hours, then complete company details, pay registration fee, and upload required documents. Final profile submission must be within 7 days of email verification. Approval is done by e-GP User Registration Desk at BPPA after document verification.
ground_truth: Go to https://eprocure.gov.bd, click “New User Registration”. Enter a unique email ID (this becomes Login-ID), create a password (min 8 characters with both alphabets and numbers), select Hint Question/Answer, Nationality, Registration Type (Tenderer/Consultant, Individual Consultant, Government Owned Enterprise, or Media), Country of Business, enter Captcha, accept Terms & Conditions, and Submit. An email with verification code is sent. Verify email within 72 hours, then complete company details, pay registration fee, and upload required documents. Final profile submission must be within 7 days of email verification. Approval is done by e-GP User Registration Desk at BPPA after document verification.
expected_citation: eGP New User Registration Manual (English), March 03, 2026, Pages 2-10, 17-27
notes: Answered from the official Tenderer/Consultant registration manual. PE-user manual does not cover this.

question: What documents are needed to create a tenderer account?

expected_answer: For National Tenderer/Consulting Firms: Company Incorporation Certificate (or Registration Document), Trade License, Valid TIN Certificate, VAT Certificate, Authorization letter from Owner for Firm/Company Admin + National ID or Passport (first 2 pages) of Authorized Admin, e-GP Registration Fee Payment Slip, one Passport size photograph of Authorized Admin. International firms have similar but some documents “If Applicable” and GST option. Government Owned Enterprise and Individual Consultant have reduced lists. Media has Identity Card + NID/Passport + photo.

notes: Directly from the registration manual document list.

question: How can I correct a wrong NID or mobile number?
expected_answer: To correct a wrong NID or mobile number: (1) For NID correction: Navigate to My Account > Edit Profile > 'Verify NID' link. question: Can I participate while a profile update is pending?
expected_answer: Participation during pending profile updates depends on what is being updated. If core verification items (NID, mobile OTP) are unverified, the system may restrict portal functionality until verification is complete. For non-critical profile changes (address update, document renewal), participation in ongoing tenders typically continues uninterrupted. However, any mandatory field or document that becomes invalid (expired Trade License, unverified NID) may prevent submission of new tenders. Best practice: Complete all profile updates and verifications before tender closing dates. Contact the e-GP Helpdesk (16575) if you face access restrictions during a pending update.

(6) Read each item carefully, verify quantities against drawings/specifications, and price each item realistically. (7) Ensure mathematical accuracy — the system may flag arithmetic errors. (8) Any items left unpriced are considered included in other rates per standard conditions.

question: Please explain: what is the difference between a tender notice and a tender document?

(5) Each category has its own STD template (Q201), evaluation criteria, and contract conditions. (6) The APP (Q81) classifies each procurement package by category. (7) Tenderers should register their business categories in their profile to receive relevant tender notifications.

expected_answer: To check the current tender closing date and time: (1) Log into e-GP and navigate to the tender detail page using the tender reference number. Submit well before the deadline. (7) The system automatically locks submissions at the exact closing time — no grace period is given.

question: When will my submitted tender be opened?
expected_answer: Tender security (earnest money) is returned under these conditions: (1) For unsuccessful bidders: within 28 days after contract signing with the winning bidder, or after tender validity period expiry, whichever is earlier. (5) If security is not returned within the prescribed period, contact the Procuring Entity and the e-GP Helpdesk (16575). (6) Tender security is NOT returned if forfeited due to bid withdrawal, refusal of NOA, or failure to furnish Performance Security.

question: What does post-qualification mean?

question: Please explain: what does post-qualification mean?
expected_answer: Post-qualification on e-GP per PPR-2008 Rule 49: (1) Post-qualification is conducted after bid evaluation to verify that the selected (lowest evaluated) bidder meets the qualification criteria specified in the TDS. (2) The TEC examines: financial standing (turnover, liquidity, credit facilities), technical experience (completed similar contracts), available equipment and key personnel, and legal standing (not debarred or in litigation). (4) Documents examined: audited financial statements, bank solvency certificates, work completion certificates, organizational charts, equipment ownership/lease records, and key personnel CVs. (5) Post-qualification is pass/fail — it determines whether the selected bidder CAN execute the contract. This differs from technical scoring which ranks bidders.

(4) If the complaint is dismissed, the PE proceeds with NOA issuance. (5) This mechanism protects tenderers' rights and ensures due process. (6) Frivolous complaints may be rejected quickly, but legitimate concerns must be properly investigated before award proceeds.

question: Please explain: can a complaint affect issuance of the Notice of Award?
expected_answer: Yes, a complaint can affect issuance of the NOA: (1) Per PPR-2008 and PPA-2006, a valid complaint triggers a procurement freeze — the PE cannot issue the NOA while the complaint is being processed (Q961). (2) The freeze remains until the complaint is resolved by the PE or the Review Panel. (3) If the complaint is upheld, the evaluation may be redone or the tender cancelled. (4) If the complaint is dismissed, the PE proceeds with NOA issuance. (5) This mechanism protects tenderers' rights and ensures due process. (6) Frivolous complaints may be rejected quickly, but legitimate concerns must be properly investigated before award proceeds.

question: Can a JV use the experience of its members?
expected_answer: Yes, a JV can use the combined experience of its members: (1) Per PPR-2008 and standard TDS conditions, the JV's qualification is assessed based on the combined capabilities of all partners. (2) Each partner's experience contributes to the JV's overall qualification. (3) The TDS (Q161) may specify: lead partner must meet a minimum percentage of experience requirements (e.g., 40-60%), and all partners collectively must meet 100%. (4) Experience certificates from individual partners' past projects are submitted and evaluated (Q401). (5) However, each specific experience claim must belong to a specific partner — not shared between partners. (6) Financial capacity (turnover, credit facilities) can also be combined per TDS rules.

question: Can a company participate in the same tender independently and as a JV member?
expected_answer: No, a company generally cannot participate in the same tender both independently and as a JV member: (1) Per PPR-2008 and standard e-GP TDS conditions (Q161), a tenderer can submit only one bid — either independently or as part of a JV. (2) Submitting both would constitute a conflict of interest and grounds for disqualification of all affected bids. category: Notice of Award and contract signing
question: What performance security is required after award?
expected_answer: Performance security on e-GP: (1) Performance security is a financial guarantee submitted by the winning bidder after receiving the Notification of Award (NOA) (Q641). (8) Failure to submit performance security within the prescribed period results in: NOA cancellation, tender security forfeiture, and the PE may award to the next-ranked bidder.

question: How are consultancy technical proposals evaluated?
expected_answer: Consultancy technical proposals are evaluated differently from works/goods: (1) Evaluation methods per PPR-2008 include: QCBS (Quality and Cost Based Selection — most common), QBS (Quality Based Selection), FBS (Fixed Budget Selection), and LCS (Least Cost Selection). question: As a tenderer, what is the difference between OTM and LTM?
expected_answer: The difference between ITB (Instructions to Bidders/Tenderers) and TDS (Tender Data Sheet): (1) ITB (also called ITT - Instructions to Tenderers) contains the general, standardized rules and procedures for bidding that apply to all tenders of a given type. (3) ITB is standard/unchanging; TDS is customized per tender by the PE.

(6) If session expires during final submission, check if the submission was registered.

question: As a tenderer, i noticed a mistake in my uploaded document just before closing. What should I do?

(7) Never wait until the last minute for submission.

question: As a tenderer, my bank guarantee expires before the new validity date. What should I do?

(6) The e-GP system's SLT calculation (Q481) and financial analysis tools help detect suspicious bidding patterns. Report suspected collusion to CPTU or the Anti-Corruption Commission.

question: Does the PE-user manual describe a validity extension request being sent to a tenderer?
expected_answer: The manual states that a Tender Validity Extension Request is sent to a tenderer when the original validity period is about to expire and more time is needed for evaluation and award.

expected_answer: The PE enters the new Tender/Proposal Validity date, the new Tender/Proposal Security Validity date, and an extension reason before submitting the request.

question: Does the PE-user manual say that a validity extension requires workflow approval?
expected_answer: Yes. The manual describes creating a workflow, specifying reviewers and initiator/approver, processing the file, and an approval action; the extension record/status is then visible in the Processed tab.
ground_truth: Yes. After submitting the request, the PE creates a Tender/Proposal Validity Extension workflow, specifies reviewers if needed, selects the initiator and approver, and processes the file through the workflow. (2) Check file format — ensure you're uploading in the accepted format (PDF, JPG, PNG). (3) Check internet speed — slow connections cause upload timeouts. Use a stable high-speed connection. (4) Clear browser cache and try again. (5) Try a different browser — Chrome is recommended. (6) Disable browser popup blockers which may interfere with upload dialogs. (7) If uploading multiple files, try one at a time. (8) Check available session time — if the session expires during upload, you'll need to re-login. (9) Restart the browser and try again. (10) If the issue persists, contact the e-GP Helpdesk (16575) with your tender reference and error details.

question: আমার tender security release হয়েছে কি না কীভাবে দেখব?
expected_answer: Tender security (earnest money) is returned under these conditions: (1) For unsuccessful bidders: within 28 days after contract signing with the winning bidder, or after tender validity period expiry, whichever is earlier. Per PPR-2008, the PE must return security promptly to unsuccessful tenderers. (2) For the winning bidder: after submission and acceptance of the Performance Security (typically 10% of contract value). (3) For all bidders: if the tender is cancelled by the PE. (4) The e-GP system's bank account integration facilitates automated security refund processing to the vendor's registered bank account (Q4 — bank details provided during registration). (5) If security is not returned within the prescribed period, contact the Procuring Entity and the e-GP Helpdesk (16575). (6) Tender security is NOT returned if forfeited due to bid withdrawal, refusal of NOA, or failure to furnish Performance Security.
